Year reported: not confirmed (likely 2024-2026).
context_as_of: [uncertain] As of Nov 2026: (1) Westlife Foodworld (McDonald's West and South) reported Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026) revenue of Rs 747 cr, +16% YoY, same-store sales growth 10.1%, digital sales above 75%, and a small net loss; it added 11 restaurants to reach 492 outlets in ~80 cities and plans 60+ openings in FY27 and 580-630 restaurants by Dec 2027 (exchange4media: https://www.exchange4media.com/marketing-news/westlife-foodworld-q2-revenue-rises-16-to-rs747-crore-digital-sales-cross-75-159467.html ; Free Press Journal: https://www.freepressjournal.in/business/westlife-foodworld-reports-16-revenue-increase-to-747-crore-in-q2-fy27-sssg-up-101 ; Sahi: https://www.sahi.com/news/westlife-foodworld-q1-profit-falls-to-6m-plans-580-630-restaurants-by-december-2027-652-PE1_CORP). (2) FY26 (Apr 2025-Mar 2026) consolidated revenue ~Rs 2,600-2,625 cr, network 478 restaurants after 48 openings; average sales per comparable store (TTM) ~Rs 6.08 cr (Whalesbook: https://www.whalesbook.com/corporate-news/English/consumer-products/Westlife-Foodworld-FY26-Revenue-indian-rupee2600-Cr-Profit-indian-rupee32-Cr-Auditors-Give-Clean-Opinion/69fc6386fba933f42cc50faa ; Quartr Q4 FY26 summary: https://quartr.com/events/westlife-foodworld-limited-505533-q4-25-26_FPNFDRjb). (3) CPRL (MMG Group) runs McDonald's in North and East India: ~245 outlets reported in early 2025 with a target of 600 by 2030, and a later report of 320+ restaurants with a target of 500+ by 2028 (Outlook Business: https://www.outlookbusiness.com/corporate/cprl-to-double-mcdonalds-store-count-to-600-by-2030-eyes-investments-up-to-150mn). Flag: CPRL is private, so its 2026 store count and per-store sales are not officially disclosed - treat ~320-340 as an estimate. Westlife's Q2 FY27 loss amount differs across outlets (Rs 2.0-2.7 cr).
regulatory_context: Mostly none material to the count. Background: (1) GST on restaurant services is 5% without input tax credit, so menu prices and AOV are GST-inclusive while reported revenue is net of GST - remove GST before converting revenue into orders. (2) FSSAI labelling and food-safety rules apply; in 2024 Maharashtra FDA action over a 'cheese analogue' at a McDonald's outlet led Westlife to relabel items - a reminder that menu naming and ingredients are regulated. (3) Delivery orders through Swiggy and Zomato carry platform commissions but are still McDonald's sales and count toward burgers sold.
public_data_anchors: 1) Westlife restaurants: 492 at end-Sep 2026 (Q2 FY27), 478 at end-Mar 2026 (FY26) - exchange4media, Oct-Nov 2026; Whalesbook, May 2026 (links above). 2) Westlife FY26 revenue ~Rs 2,625 cr (net of GST) and average sales per comparable store (TTM) ~Rs 6.08 cr (Whalesbook / Quartr, May 2026). 3) Westlife Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 747 cr, +16% YoY; SSSG 10.1%; digital >75% of sales (exchange4media, Nov 2026). 4) CPRL North and East: 245 outlets (early 2025), 320+ in a later report; targets 500-600 by 2028-2030 (Outlook Business, 2025). 5) [uncertain] Average order value at McDonald's India is not disclosed each quarter; Rs 250-350 for dine-in and takeaway and Rs 350-450 for delivery is a reasonable assumption based on menu prices (McAloo Tikki ~Rs 60-70, McChicken ~Rs 150-170, Maharaja Mac ~Rs 250-300, meals Rs 250-400). 6) India population ~145 crore (frameworks.md anchor).
framework_applied: Guesstimates: Clarify, Pick framework, Constraints/MECE, Calculate, Sanity check (frameworks.md section 6). Step 1 Clarify - count burgers (including McAloo Tikki, McChicken, Maharaja Mac, McVeggie, Filet-o-Fish) sold by all McDonald's restaurants in India over a year (FY27 run-rate), across dine-in, takeaway, drive-thru and delivery; exclude wraps, nuggets, fries, McCafe and desserts. Step 2 Pick framework - bottom-up: stores x orders per store per day x burgers per order x 365, with orders anchored on Westlife's published revenue (revenue / AOV) rather than invented footfall. Step 3 Constraints and MECE - segment by franchisee (Westlife West and South vs. CPRL North and East), because store productivity differs; within orders, split by channel (dine-in/takeaway vs. delivery) since AOV and burgers per order differ; natural constraint = kitchen throughput (~1 burger a minute per assembly line at the peak). Step 4 Calculate - Westlife ~485 stores x ~2.2 lakh burgers = ~10.7 crore; CPRL ~330 stores x ~1.6 lakh = ~5.3 crore; total ~16 crore burgers a year (range 12-20 crore). Step 5 Sanity check - revenue-share test (burgers at ~Rs 140 net each are ~50% of system sales), per-store throughput (~600 burgers a day, ~40 an hour) and a 1-in-N test (~0.11 burgers per Indian per year).

clarifying_questions.q: Which period - the last financial year or a current run-rate?
clarifying_questions.a: A current annual run-rate, roughly FY27.

clarifying_questions.q: Does 'McDonald's India' include both franchisees - Westlife in the West and South and CPRL in the North and East?
clarifying_questions.a: Yes, all McDonald's restaurants in India.

clarifying_questions.q: What counts as a burger - only buns with a patty, or also wraps, McSpicy rolls and breakfast muffins?
clarifying_questions.a: Burgers and breakfast muffins in a bun count. Wraps, nuggets, fries, McCafe and desserts don't.

clarifying_questions.q: Does a burger in a combo meal count the same as a standalone burger?
clarifying_questions.a: Yes, one burger is one burger regardless of how it's sold.

clarifying_questions.q: Do delivery orders through Swiggy and Zomato count?
Can I use public financials, like Westlife's revenue and store counts?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Let's do a guesstimate. How many McDonald's burgers are sold in India each year?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: A few clarifications. Is this a current annual run-rate, and does it cover both franchisees - Westlife in the West and South, and CPRL, the MMG Group company, in the North and East?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Yes, current run-rate, all of McDonald's India.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: What counts as a burger? I'd include McAloo Tikki, McChicken, McVeggie, Maharaja Mac and breakfast muffins, but exclude wraps, nuggets, fries, McCafe and desserts. And burgers inside combo meals count?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: That's right on all counts. Delivery counts too.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text:
My approach: bottom-up. Burgers = stores x orders per store per day x burgers per order x 365. Rather than guessing footfall, I'll anchor orders on revenue, since Westlife is listed: orders = sales per store / average order value. Then I segment by franchisee because store productivity differs, and by order type for burgers per order. Structure:
  Burgers per year
  |- Westlife (West and South): stores x (sales per store / AOV) x burgers per order x 365
  |- CPRL (North and East): same formula, lower per-store sales
  Burgers per order = burger orders x 1 + group orders x 2.5 + non-burger orders x 0

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Why not top-down from population?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Top-down needs 'how many Indians eat McDonald's and how often', which is two weak assumptions. Store counts and Westlife revenue are public, so bottom-up needs fewer guesses.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Stores: Westlife had 492 restaurants at end-September 2026, up from 478 in March, so ~485 on average this year. CPRL was ~245 in early 2025 and reported 320+ later, so ~330. Total ~815 McDonald's in India.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Fine. Now sales per store.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Westlife's FY26 revenue was ~Rs 2,625 crore, and average sales per comparable store is about Rs 6 crore a year. CPRL is private; its stores are newer and it has fewer high-traffic highway and mall flagships, so I'll take ~70% of that, ~Rs 4.2 crore.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: And average order value?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Menu prices: McAloo Tikki ~Rs 65, McChicken ~Rs 160, a meal Rs 250-400, McCafe coffee ~Rs 150. Delivery baskets are bigger. Blended, net of the 5% GST, ~Rs 280 at Westlife and ~Rs 270 at CPRL. So Westlife orders per store = 6 crore / 280 = ~2.1 lakh a year, ~590 a day. CPRL = 4.2 crore / 270 = ~1.55 lakh a year, ~425 a day.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: How many burgers in an order?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Three types. About 55% of orders are a single person's burger or burger meal - 1 burger. About 20% are group or family orders, often delivery - ~2.5 burgers. About 25% have no burger at all - coffee, McFlurry, fries, wraps, nuggets. Weighted: 0.55 + 0.5 + 0 = ~1.05 burgers per order.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Calculate.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Westlife: 590 orders x 1.05 = ~620 burgers per store per day; x 485 stores x 365 = ~11 crore. CPRL: 425 x 1.05 = ~445 a day; x 330 x 365 = ~5.4 crore. Total ~16 crore burgers a year - about 160 million, or ~4.4 lakh a day across India.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Sanity-check it.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Three ways. Throughput: ~600 burgers a day over ~15 operating hours is ~40 an hour, with maybe 80-100 at the lunch and dinner peak - one or two assembly lines can do that, so it's plausible. Revenue share: 16 crore burgers at ~Rs 140 net average, after combo allocation, is ~Rs 2,250 crore - about half of the ~Rs 4,300 crore combined system sales, which fits a burger chain where fries, drinks, McCafe and desserts make up the rest. 1-in-N: ~0.11 burgers per Indian per year, or about one every nine years per person - low, but McDonald's is concentrated in ~80 cities for Westlife and a similar footprint for CPRL, so for urban middle-class customers it's a few a year.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: What's your biggest uncertainty?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: CPRL's store productivity - it's private, so its per-store sales could be Rs 3.5-5 crore, swinging the total by +/-1.5 crore. Second is AOV: if the blended AOV is Rs 330 instead of 280, orders and burgers fall by ~15%.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Does the 16% revenue growth change anything?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: It means the run-rate is rising: Westlife's Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 747 crore annualises to ~Rs 3,000 crore, and same-store sales grew 10%. If half of that growth is price and mix, burger units grow ~8-10% a year, so FY28 would be ~17-18 crore.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Summarise.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: McDonald's sells about 16 crore - 160 million - burgers a year in India: ~11 crore through Westlife's ~485 stores in the West and South, and ~5 crore through CPRL's ~330 stores in the North and East. That's about 600 burgers per store per day, and burgers are roughly half of system sales.

answer_and_recommendation: Estimate: ~16 crore (160 mn) McDonald's burgers a year in India (range 12-20 crore), ~4.4 lakh a day. Ranked components: (1) Westlife (West and South): ~485 stores x ~590 orders a day (Rs 6 cr sales / Rs 280 AOV) x 1.05 burgers x 365 = ~11 crore; (2) CPRL (North and East): ~330 stores x ~425 orders x 1.05 x 365 = ~5.4 crore; (3) the swing factor is burgers per order (~1.05, driven by the ~25% of orders with no burger and ~20% group orders). Risks in the estimate: CPRL store count and per-store sales are not disclosed (+/-1.5 crore); AOV assumption (+/-15%); the unit count grows ~8-10% a year with 60+ Westlife openings and CPRL expansion. Closing line: 'About 16 crore burgers a year - roughly 600 per store per day across ~815 restaurants - anchored on Westlife's ~Rs 6 crore sales per store, and it checks out because burgers come to about half of McDonald's India's ~Rs 4,300 crore system sales.'
counter_metrics_guardrails: Pure guesstimate - sanity checks used instead of guardrails: (1) Kitchen throughput constraint: ~620 burgers per store per day = ~40 an hour over 15 hours and ~80-100 at the peak hour - within one or two assembly lines' capacity; 3,000 a day would break this test. (2) Revenue-share ratio test: 16 crore burgers x ~Rs 140 net = ~Rs 2,250 cr, ~50% of combined system sales of ~Rs 4,300 cr (Westlife ~Rs 3,000 cr annualised + CPRL ~Rs 1,350-1,400 cr estimated) - plausible for a burger-led menu. (3) 1-in-N test: ~0.11 burgers per Indian a year; restricted to ~20-25 crore urban middle-class consumers in McDonald's cities, ~0.7 a year each - reasonable for an occasional-treat QSR brand. (4) Peak-day stress test: on a delivery-app sale day or a long weekend, daily burgers may rise 1.5-2x to ~7-9 lakh - still within store capacity.

follow_up_twists.twist: PhonePe angle: what share of these burgers is paid via UPI, and how many UPI transactions is that?
follow_up_twists.response: Roughly 60-70% of non-delivery orders in Indian metros are paid by UPI, and delivery is paid in-app (also mostly UPI); at ~2.4 lakh orders a day nationally, that's ~1.5-1.7 lakh UPI transactions a day, or ~5.5-6 crore a year - a rounding error against India's ~20 bn+ monthly UPI transactions.

follow_up_twists.twist: How would the number change if McDonald's India added a Rs 49 burger value menu?
follow_up_twists.response: Units rise faster than revenue - if the value menu adds 0.1 burgers per order and pulls in 5% more orders, burgers rise ~15% to ~18-19 crore while revenue grows only ~5-7%; I'd watch AOV and margin as counter-metrics.

follow_up_twists.twist: Estimate Burger King India's burgers per year using the same method.
follow_up_twists.response: Restaurant Brands Asia has ~500+ India stores at roughly Rs 3.5-4 crore sales per store and a lower AOV of ~Rs 230 with more burger-heavy orders (~1.2 per order), so ~500 x 450 x 1.2 x 365 = ~10 crore - about 60% of McDonald's.

common_pitfalls: Forgetting there are two franchisees - using only Westlife's ~490 stores misses the ~320-340 CPRL stores in the North and East and undercounts by about a third.

Assuming every order contains one burger - McCafe coffee, McFlurry, fries-only and wrap orders are a meaningful share, while family and delivery orders carry several burgers; the weighted ~1.05 is the honest number.
Converting revenue to orders without removing the 5% GST, or using the McAloo Tikki price as the AOV - both inflate the order count by 2-4x.

Starting top-down from 145 crore Indians with an arbitrary 'x% eat McDonald's monthly' - it ignores that McDonald's is present in only ~150-200 cities, and the result cannot be reconciled with public revenue.
